title: Token-affinity prefetch lanes and PCIe coalescer for paged KV cache
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Implement a token-affinity prefetch lanes subsystem and a PCIe coalescer to reduce PCIe transfer overhead and smoothing GPU DRAM residency for the paged/block KV cache. This ticket describes the end-to-end design, prototype, metrics, and rollout plan for a policy that groups adjacent KV page fetches into bandwidth-aware lanes tied to token-affinity windows, and coalesces GPU-host transfers to reduce PCIe scatter and DMA overhead.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end prototype reduces PCIe transfer count by >=20% on our standard large-chat workload without increasing p95 token latency by >5%.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
- Add a lightweight lane abstraction in the KV fetcher that groups requests by token-affinity (recently touched tokens / request traces) and sequence-window similarity. Lanes maintain a small in-memory ring of pending page fetch intents to be issued in a single coalesced DMA batch when thresholds are met.
- Implement a PCIe coalescer in the host-side staging layer: coalescer merges adjacent GPU page requests by physical address range, rewrites contiguous host buffers, and issues a single cuMemcpyAsync or equivalent (NCCL/GPUDirect path retained).
- Integrate lane scheduling with the continuous-batcher so that lane flushes align to batch boundaries where possible to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Add bandwidth-aware eviction tie-in: if sustained PCIe bandwidth > configured watermark, expand lane flush thresholds and favor eviction of low-affinity slabs to free DRAM.
- Safety: ensure individual critical prefetches (small latency-sensitive requests) can bypass lane coalescing via a high-priority path.
- Observability: expose lane metric counters (lane_count, coalesced_transfers, avg_transfer_bytes, flush_latency_ms) and a PCIe bandwidth gauge per GPU device.
- Toggle via runtime feature-flag (kv.prefetch_lanes.enabled) and per-customer config for Dedicated/Private tiers.
decisions: Use token-affinity (recent activity heuristics) + sequence-window similarity for grouping rather than purely physical adjacency to preserve workload locality benefits.
Implement host-side coalescer rather than GPU kernel-level merges to keep changes isolated from runtime kernel scheduling and reduce driver complexity.
Make lane flush thresholds adaptive to measured PCIe bandwidth and batch alignment to avoid increasing p95 latency under load.
Keep a bypass path for single-page critical fetches to preserve interactive latency SLOs.
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Spike complete. Implemented prototype lane abstraction and verified coalescing logic on unit tests (local GPU). Measured naive coalescing reduces transfer count by ~28% on synthetic sequential page access pattern.

2026-02-25: Integrated lane flush alignment with continuous batcher; observed a 9% p95 latency increase when naive flushes triggered mid-batch. Increasing flush alignment to end-of-batch reduced p95 impact to ~1.6%.
2026-03-02: Added PCIe bandwidth watermark and adaptive flush thresholds. On 2x oversubscription tests, adaptive policy reduced DMA retries and recovered tail latency to within SLOs.

2026-03-06: End-to-end benchmark on large-chat workload: 12% p95 token latency reduction for heavy KV-cache hit-rate scenarios due to fewer PCIe stalls; overall PCIe transfer count down 22%. Observability dashboard draft: https://go/redwood/dashboards/kv-prefetch-lanes
2026-03-10: Opened PR linking prototype into staging runtime (gh: redwood-inference/runtime#1428). Running canary on dedicated pool with feature flag enabled for internal CI tenants.
2026-03-12: Noted suboptimal behavior for multi-tenant bursts where lane grouping caused cross-tenant PCIe bursts; added per-tenant isolation to lanes in the latest patch.
comments: Ravi Mehta (2026-02-20): Spike looks promising. Need to ensure we don't regress Dedicated latency SLAs for multi-tenant hosts.
Priya Singh (SRE, 2026-02-28): Add a metric for 'coalesced_transfer_backpressure' so SRE can alert on sustained bandwidth saturation.
Design review (Mar 3): Approved subject to per-tenant isolation and a global guardrail for DMA rate limiting.
QA (2026-03-09): Identified flaky behavior when small pages (<2KB) were aggregated leading to extra memcpy overhead; added min-aggregation-size param to coalescer.
